description: Somos NOSTOC SPACE, un equipo orientado a la ciencia, la ingeniería, la tecnología y la exploración espacial. Nos apasiona desarrollar soluciones innovadoras mediante la programación, electrónica, inteligencia artificial, automatización y análisis de datos. Buscamos personas creativas, comprometidas y con ganas de aprender, compartir conocimientos y trabajar colaborativamente para afrontar desafíos utilizando los recursos y datos proporcionados por la NASA. ¡Las grandes ideas no tienen límites!
summary: NOSTOC SPACE is an automated hydroponic system designed to cultivate cushuro (*Nostoc sphaericum*), an ancestral Andean microorganism with significant nutritional value, outside its natural high-altitude lagoon environment. Our prototype integrates three cultivation modules, a 20-liter storage tank, water recirculation through two pumps and an activated carbon filter, four nutrient-dosing containers, and a motorized movement mechanism. An ESP32-based control system monitors key water parameters, including pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), temperature, and dissolved oxygen, enabling more controlled cultivation conditions. The project also incorporates NASA POWER climate data as a resource for understanding environmental conditions and planning cultivation cycles. By combining mechatronics, automation, and NASA satellite data, NOSTOC SPACE aims to promote efficient water use, support sustainable food production, and explore new possibilities for cultivating nutritious Andean resources in controlled environments.
details:
NOSTOC SPACE is an intelligent hydroponic cultivation system designed to reproduce and control the environmental conditions required for growing cushuro (Nostoc sphaericum) outside its natural high-altitude lagoon habitat. The prototype consists of three cultivation modules supported by a motorized mechanical structure, a 20-liter storage tank, two water pumps (impulsion and return), an activated carbon filter, and four nutrient-dosing containers. Its operation is based on a water recirculation system that distributes the cultivation solution through the modules. An ESP32-based control architecture integrates sensors to monitor essential parameters, including pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), temperature, water flow, and dissolved oxygen. The system also incorporates a motorized movement mechanism that allows the cultivation modules to move in a controlled sequence. NASA POWER climate data provides additional environmental information to support the analysis and planning of cultivation cycles.

The main benefits are improved water management through recirculation, controlled cultivation conditions, reduced dependence on natural lagoon environments, and the potential for sustainable production of a nutrient-rich Andean resource. Our project's creativity lies in combining hydroponics, mechatronics, automated nutrient management, mechanical movement, and NASA satellite-derived climate information in a modular cultivation system. The development considers several critical factors: water quality, nutrient concentration, temperature stability, oxygen availability, environmental conditions, mechanical reliability, energy consumption, and ease of maintenance. The hardware includes an ESP32 microcontroller, pH and TDS sensors, temperature and dissolved oxygen sensors, water-flow sensors, pumps, a stepper motor, and a water filtration system. Mechanical components were designed using CAD tools, while the electronic control and monitoring architecture uses embedded programming and an MQTT-based communication approach. Our long-term vision is to develop a scalable cultivation solution that contributes to food sustainability and demonstrates how Andean biological resources could be cultivated in controlled environments, potentially supporting future space agriculture research.
